newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Drug smuggling through Tajikistan rises sharply.
newsitem.headline: Drug smuggling through Tajikistan rises sharply.

text.p: Russian border guards in Tajikistan said on Tuesday they had seen a marked increase in drug smuggling along the former Soviet republic's border with Afghanistan.

"In the last week alone, Russian border guard units in Tajikistan have seized more than 65 kg (143 lbs) of narcotics, brought in from Afghanistan," Russia's Federal Border Service said in a statement in the Tajik capital Dushanbe.
It said border guards had prevented about 15 armed smugglers trying to cross from Afghanistan into Tajikistan late on Monday.

In June, Russia's border guards said they had seized over 800 kg (1,760 lbs) of narcotics, mostly raw opium, since the begining of the year in Tajikistan, now tentatively emerging from a four-year civil war.
Russia deploys about 20,000 troops in the Central Asian state, by agreement with the government. They carry out peacekeeping duties and guard the frontiers with Afghanistan and China.
The troops clash regularly with drug smugglers who sneak across the treacherous Pyandzh River from Afghanistan into Tajikistan.

Porous borders and a decline in law and order since the Soviet Union collapsed have seen a large increase in the quantity of drugs from war-ravaged Afghanistan that are smuggled across former Soviet Central Asia to markets in western Europe.
